Gain-of-function (GOF) mutations or those with normal function are found in patients with Neurodevelopmental Disorder with Involuntary Movements (NEDIM).
Gain-of-function (GOF) mutations or those with normal function are found in patients with Neurodevelopmental Disorder with Involuntary Movements (NEDIM).
A mouse Gnao1 knock-in GOF mutation (G203R) was created by CRISPR/Cas9 methods.
A previously reported GOF mutant mouse knock-in (Gnao1+/G184S), which has not been found in patients, was also studied for comparison.

claims.object_text: Gnao1+/G203R mice (viable; gain weight comparably to controls)
claims.quote: Gnao1+/G203R mutant mice are viable and gain weight comparably to controls.
Grip strength was decreased in both males and females.
Male Gnao1+/G203R mice were strongly affected in movement assays (RotaRod and DigiGait) while females were not.
Male Gnao1+/G203R mice also showed enhanced seizure propensity in the pentylenetetrazole kindling test.
Mice with a G184S GOF knock-in also showed movement-related behavioral phenotypes but females were more strongly affected than males.

claims.object_text: phenocopy of heterozygous GNAO1 G203R patients (movement disorder and mild epilepsy)
claims.quote: Gnao1+/G203R mice phenocopy children with heterozygous GNAO1 G203R mutations, showing both movement disorder and a relatively mild epilepsy pattern.
